newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up on technical rally.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up on technical rally.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures ended higher across the board Tuesday in a moderate session, with some technical buying boosting the complex after downside momentum stalled early, industry sources said.
June gained 6.1 cents to close at $2.142 per million British thermal units. July settled 4.4 cents higher at $2.165. Other deferreds ended up by 1.2 to 4.2 cents.

"There was a lack of liquidity and the locals were long and pushed it up. We held support early, then hit some stops above $2.11 (basis June)," said one East Coast trader, noting futures climbed today above May Hub cash in the $2.10 area.

But with mostly seasonal weather forecast this week for much of the nation, some still expected May to open on a soft note, noting a lack of cooling demand in the South and the loss of recent heating loads in the Midwest and Northeast.
Early estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA inventory report still ranged from a draw of 10 bcf to a build of 30 bcf.

Technical traders agreed the market remained range-bound, with next support in June at $2.03, which roughly coincides with short-term trendline support in the low-$2s. Resistance was still seen at $2.18, $2.24 and then at $2.33. They said a break below $2 (basis June) could trigger a flood of selling, noting funds and speculators have been big buyers recently.
"The oil rally spilled into the gas ring, but the buyers weren't industry. They were mostly locals and funds," said one Midwest trader.

In the May cash, Gulf Coast prices notionally held steady in the $2.04-09 range. May Midcon pipes slid a couple of cents to the low-$1.90s. New York city gate gas for May was several cents lower in the mid-to-high $2.30s on milder weather there.
The NYMEX 12-month Hub strip gained 3.4 cents to $2.231. NYMEX said 31,777 Hub contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 19,582.

On the KCBT, June finished 4.5 cents higher at $1.98, while deferreds ended steady to up 3.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.6 cents to 16.2 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 465 lots changed hands, up from Monday's total of 195.
